name: Mam cai
summary: Mắm cái is a salty dipping bowl, traced to Cham seafarers who salted fish before going to sea. It shares that salt with Huế mắm nêm, and the aroma is different enough that a practiced eater can tell them apart.
origin: The communes around My Son, and Quảng Nam in the ministry article of 7 Feb 2025.
history: The sanctuary essay says the bowl comes from Cham people who salted fish before going to sea, and that central Vietnamese cooking uses fish sauce where another region would set out soy.
taste: A jar of Huế mắm nêm and a bowl of Quảng Nam mắm cái share a salty taste, and the aroma is different enough that a practiced eater can tell them apart.
where: The sanctuary essay places the bowl in the communes around My Son. The 7 Feb 2025 ministry article places it in Quảng Nam.
seoTitle: Mam cai — a salty dip around My Son
seoDescription: Mắm cái is a salty dipping bowl traced to Cham seafarers. The salt is close to Huế mắm nêm, and the aroma is different.
